questions.label: Illustration 1
questions.text: Assume that a body is displaced from $\vec{r}_A = (2\text{m}, 4\text{m}, -6\text{m})$ to $\vec{r}_B = (6\hat{i} - 4\hat{j} + 2\hat{k})\text{ m}$ under a constant force $\vec{F} = (2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - \hat{k})\text{ N}$. Calculate the total work done.

questions.label: Illustration 2
questions.text: A block of total mass $5\text{ kg}$ is being raised vertically upwards with the help of a string attached to it and it rises with an acceleration of $2\text{ m/s}^2$. Find the work done due to the tension in the string if the block rises by $2.5\text{ m}$. Also, calculate the work done due to gravity and the net work done. ($g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2$).

questions.label: Illustration 3
questions.text: A force $F = (10 + 0.50x)\text{ N}$ is observed to act on a particle in the $x$ direction, where $x$ is in meters. Find the actual work done by this force during a displacement from $x = 0$ to $x = 2.0\text{ m}$.

questions.label: Illustration 4
questions.text:
A block of mass $4\text{ kg}$ slides down a plane inclined at $37^\circ$ with the horizontal. The length of the plane is $3\text{ m}$. The coefficient of sliding friction between the block and the plane is $\mu = 0.2$. Find:
1. The work done due to gravity,
2. The work done by the frictional force,
3. The work done by the normal reaction between the block and the plane.  
($g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2, \sin 37^\circ = 0.6, \cos 37^\circ = 0.8$).

questions.label: Illustration 5
questions.text: A block of mass $m$ slides down a fixed smooth inclined plane of inclination angle $\theta$ and length $l$. Calculate the magnitude of instantaneous power developed by the gravitational force when the block reaches the bottom.

questions.label: Illustration 6
questions.text: A particle of mass $m$ is moving in a circular path of constant radius $r$ such that its centripetal acceleration $a_c$ varies with time $t$ as $a_c = k^2 r t^2$, where $k$ is a constant. The power delivered to the particle by the net force acting on it is:

questions.label: Illustration 11
questions.text: A uniform flexible chain of length $l$ and mass $m$ overhangs a smooth horizontal table with two-thirds ($2l/3$) of its length lying on the table. Find the kinetic energy of the chain as it completely slips off the table.

questions.label: Illustration 12
questions.text: A block of mass $m$ is pushed against a light spring of spring constant $k$ fixed at one end to a rigid vertical wall. The block slides on a frictionless horizontal table. The natural length of the spring is $L_0$. The spring is compressed to half its natural length ($x_{\text{init}} = L_0/2$) and the block is released from rest. Find the velocity of the block as a function of its distance $x$ from the wall.
